chunks: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ghalib al-Anmati narrated to us, saying: Abu Amr Ahmad ibn al-Hasn ibn Ghazwan informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

While a man was lying on his back, looking at the sky and the stars, and saying: 'By Allah, verily you have a Lord who is your Creator. O Allah, forgive me,' Allah, the Mighty and High, looked at him and forgave him.
The compiler of this book said: And Allah, the Mighty and High, has said: 'Or do they not look into the Kingdom of the Heavens and the Earth and whatever things Allah created?'

What is meant by this is: Have they not contemplated the Kingdom of the Heavens and the Earth and the wonders of their creation? Have they not looked at it with the gaze of one who reasons and reflects, so that they may know from what they see that which Allah established regarding the Heavens and the Earth, despite their great size and heaviness, supported without pillars and settled without tools? Thus they may deduce from this that their Creator, Master, and Sustainer does not resemble bodies, nor do the gods taken by the disbelievers besides Allah resemble Him, since bodies cannot sustain the smallest of particles in the air without pillars or tools. Through this, they recognize the Creator of the Heavens and the Earth and all other bodies, and recognize that He does not resemble them, nor do they resemble Him, in the power and dominion of Allah.

As for the Kingdom of the Heavens and the Earth, it is Allah's dominion over them and His power upon them. What is meant is: Have they not looked and contemplated the Heavens and the Earth, seeing that Allah created them upon what they witness them to be upon, so that they may know that Allah is their Master and the One with power over them, because they are owned and created, and are within His power, authority, and dominion? He made their looking at the Heavens and the Earth and the creation of Allah for them as a look into their Kingdom and into Allah's dominion over them, because Allah does not create except what He owns and has power over. And by His words 'and whatever things Allah created,' He means: from the types of His creation, so they may deduce from this that Allah is their Creator and is more worthy of Lordship than the created, newly formed bodies.

key_terms.الْمُقْتَدِرُ عَلَيْهَا: The One with power over it
key_terms.مَلَكُوتِ: Kingdom/Dominion (the unseen realm of control and power)

ai.seo_question: How does contemplating the sky lead to forgiveness and understanding of Tawhid?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to illustrate the efficacy of *tadabbur* (contemplation) as a path to *tawhid*, where observing the cosmos's structural integrity without visible supports serves as empirical proof of Allah's absolute sovereignty. The commentary distinguishes between the physical 'heavens and earth' and their metaphysical 'kingdom' (*malakut*), emphasizing that created bodies cannot sustain themselves, thereby proving the Creator's transcendence over material limitations. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on using rational observation of nature to affirm divine unity and distinctness from idols.
